<description>
**Problem:** The oversized-script fallback appends `OP_RETURN` to the destination instead of replacing it. If the destination already contains an unfinished push, the appended byte becomes pushed data and the result can remain spendable.

**Fix:** Replace the destination with `OP_RETURN` rather than appending it.

Found while reviewing #36280. This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6396973053 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK 426f29c3f1639e4c97be63cdf4c2e76bb86b39dd

I decoded 1307 compressed scripts (raw sizes 0 to 39 and from just under `MAX_SCRIPT_SIZE` to 200000, truncated streams, every special type) into a fresh target and five reused ones, a P2PKH among them, and compared each result with what a library I maintain decodes from the same bytes. On the base, every complete oversized script decoded into a reused target keeps the old bytes and appends `OP_RETURN` (35 decodes). On this head every raw and oversized case matches for every target.

One path still depends on the target: an uncompressed P2PK (type 4 or 5) whose x is not on the curve leaves a reused target untouched, so a P2PKH stays a P2PKH. #36280 makes that path throw. Its `compressor.h` change merges cleanly with this one; only `compress_tests.cpp` conflicts. With both applied, no decode in the set depends on what the target held before. I can share the vectors and the test.
</new_statements>
